status.line: Shows whether Hide is running, with its process, its port and how many windows are connected to it.

stop.line: Stops Hide's background service on this machine, so Hide is no longer running until you open it again.

version.line: Shows the version and commit of this Hide build.

guide.line: Prints the guide Hide gives an agent in its pane: letters, agents, the operator's screen and Project Memory.

issue help.line: Prints the steps for reporting a bug in Hide itself to its GitHub issues, which an agent follows once you agree.

contract.line: Prints the commands that tools call and the answers they get, as JSON, so a tool can check it matches this build.

request send.line: Sends a letter from an agent's pane to another agent, which keeps the reply and retries the letter without sending it twice.
request send.example: hide request send parent-name --kind progress --intent task-plan-1 --body 'Plan: core first, then web.'

request reply.line: Answers a letter you received, so the sender gets your answer with the letter it was about.
request reply.example: hide request reply letter-1 --intent task-answer-1 --body 'The check passed.'

request ack.line: Records that you received a letter, which is the receipt the sender waits for.

request cancel.line: Cancels a letter you sent that is still waiting for its answer.

request show.line: Opens one letter in full, including a letter that an inbox bundle only lists by its id.

inbox.line: Lists the letters waiting for you and the ones that came back undelivered, with the command that marks them taken.

watch start.line: Starts a watch on an agent, so you get a letter when that agent has been quiet for too long.

watch assign.line: Hands a watch to another observer, so that agent's quiet-time letters go to the new one.

watch stop.line: Stops a watch, so its observer no longer gets letters about that agent.

watch list.line: Lists the watches that are running and who observes each one.

agent register.line: Adds an agent that you started yourself in a Hide pane to Hide's list of agents, under the parent you name.

agent list.line: Lists the agents Hide knows, with the machine each runs on and whether it is running, asleep or ended.

agent show.line: Shows one agent: its id, its parent, its machine, and what it is doing and waiting on now.

agent ask-human.line: Tells Hide that a step needs a person, such as a sign-in or a permission, so the operator is asked and the agent stops until it is done.

agent end.line: Ends an agent and closes its pane, keeping its conversation so the operator can resume it; with --keep-pane only the agent's registration ends.

agent sleep.line: Puts a resting agent to sleep: its process ends, its conversation is kept, and a request or block letter wakes it again.

agent archive.line: Saves an agent's conversation and closes its panes, so the operator can resume it later from the archive.

agent catalog.line: Lists the agent kinds and profiles you can start here, with the models and efforts each one takes.

agent profile list.line: Lists the profiles on this machine: each one is a way to start an agent, with its own account folder.

agent profile add.line: Adds a profile for an agent kind, such as a second account with its own folder, that a start can then choose with --profile.
agent profile add.example: hide agent profile add claude work --account ~/.claude-work

agent profile edit.line: Changes a profile's name, program or environment variables; the built-in default profile cannot be edited.
agent profile edit.example: hide agent profile edit claude work --rename client

agent profile default.line: Makes a profile the one an agent starts with when nothing else chooses a profile.
agent profile default.example: hide agent profile default claude work

agent profile remove.line: Removes a profile that no running or sleeping agent uses; the built-in default profile cannot be removed.
agent profile remove.example: hide agent profile remove claude work

agent profile reinstall.line: Installs Hide's hooks into a profile's account folder again, to repair a profile whose hooks are missing.
agent profile reinstall.example: hide agent profile reinstall claude work

agent spawn.line: Starts a new agent in a tab of its own, or beside your pane with --beside, and gives it a brief to start on.
agent spawn.example: hide agent spawn --parent here --name review-1 --intent review-1 --kind claude --repo ~/projects/app --branch review-1 --brief 'Review the diff and report.'

ps.line: Shows the panes and agents Hide runs, as a tree of checkouts, tabs and panes; --here keeps only this project.

device list.line: Lists the devices connected to this Hide, with each one's state and whatever it is waiting on from you.

device add.line: Adds a computer you reach over SSH as a device, so Hide can use its folders, Git and terminals.

device remove.line: Forgets a device; its panes and agents keep running there.

device retry.line: Tries to connect a device again, and with --wait waits until it connects or the attempt fails.

mission help.line: Prints the guide for a mission's Conductor, the agent that plans a mission and starts the agents that do its work.

mission create.line: Creates a new mission with a title, which a plan and its agents then carry out.
mission create.example: hide mission create --title 'Fix the lens filter'

mission plan.line: Sets a mission's plan from a JSON file: its nodes, their order, their checks and the worker for each.

mission node.line: Updates one node of a mission's plan, such as its status, its branch, its pull request or its worker.
mission node.example: hide mission node fix-1487 --status working --agent-id agent-7

mission record.line: Records one finish line of a node as passed or failed, with the evidence that shows it.
mission record.example: hide mission record fix-1487 c1 --pass --evidence 'The lens keeps its filter after a reload.'

mission skip.line: Marks one finish line of a node as skipped, with a reason, so the node can go on.
mission skip.example: hide mission skip cause c2 --reason 'Covered by the next node.'

mission defect.line: Reopens an earlier node with a defect that a later node found, so its worker can fix it.
mission defect.example: hide mission defect fix-1487 --found-by together --line 'The lens loses its filter after a reload.'

mission gate.line: Settles a place the operator asked to check, using the operator's own words, so the node can finish.

mission start.line: Starts a planned mission once the operator has approved its plan, so its nodes begin.

mission decide.line: Puts a question for the operator on the mission's map, or clears it with --clear once it is answered.
mission decide.example: hide mission decide --line 'Ship the lens fix in this pull request?' --option yes --option no

mission delay.line: Holds new starts for a mission with a reason, such as usage near a limit, until you clear it with --clear.
mission delay.example: hide mission delay --line 'Usage is close to the limit.'

mission close.line: Closes a mission as done, as waiting for merge, or as cancelled, with a report of what it did.

mission reopen.line: Opens a closed mission again so its nodes can continue.

mission take.line: Takes over a mission whose Conductor is gone, so you become the one that runs its plan.

mission show.line: Shows a mission as text, or one node in full, or the whole record as JSON with --json.

mission list.line: Lists the missions in this Hide, with their status and their Conductor.

mission settings.line: Shows the mission defaults: how many agents may run at once, the default scope and the worker candidates.

task help.line: Prints the guide for keeping your own plan of steps, which Hide shows as a map beside your pane.

task set.line: Puts up the steps of your task, so the operator can see where you are on the map beside your pane.

task node.line: Changes one step of your plan: its status, a line about it, or the pull request or file that finishes it.
task node.example: hide task node spec --status done --file docs/spec.md

task approve.line: Approves a plan that was sent to the operator for review, so the work can go on.

task drop.line: Drops a plan the operator asked you not to carry out.

task show.line: Shows an agent's plan, with the status of each of its steps.

pane read.line: Prints the last lines of a pane, unwrapped, so you can see what its program last showed.

pane send.line: Types text into a pane, or presses keys in it such as Escape or Enter.

pane open.line: Opens a new pane beside your own pane and runs a command in it, without moving your keyboard focus.
pane open.example: hide pane open --beside -- npm run dev

agent read.line: Prints the last lines of an agent's pane, so you can see what the agent last showed.

workspace purpose.line: Sets the one-line purpose of your checkout, which the sidebar shows; it can be 40 characters at most.
workspace purpose.example: hide workspace purpose 'Fix the lens filter'

workspace info.line: Shows the workspace and checkout Hide has for this folder, and the device they run on.

file open.line: Shows a file to the operator in Hide's View, as a tab, until they look at it.

diff open.line: Shows the changes to a file to the operator in Hide's View, as a tab, until they look at it.

browser open.line: Opens a web page, or a local file, as a browser tab in Hide's View, so the operator can look at it.

browser connect.line: Asks Hide for the browser display of this checkout, or the one you name with --display, and prints its answer.

browser snapshot.line: Reads the page in a browser display as a list of its elements, each with a ref you can act on.

browser click.line: Clicks an element of the page, by its ref, by its visible text, or by a point.

browser fill.line: Fills a form field of the page with a value.

browser press.line: Presses a key in the page, such as Enter, Tab or Escape.

browser hover.line: Moves the pointer over an element of the page, so a menu or tooltip can show.

browser drag.line: Drags from one element or point of the page to another.

browser scroll.line: Scrolls the page up or down, or to an element.

browser wait.line: Waits until a text or an element appears in the page, or disappears with --gone, and stops at a timeout.

browser screenshot.line: Saves a picture of the page, or of one element with --ref, to a file.

browser eval.line: Runs a JavaScript expression in the page and prints its result.

browser console.line: Shows the messages the page logged to its console, newest first.

browser network.line: Shows the network requests the page made, with their timing but not their headers or bodies.

browser help.line: Prints the guide for driving a browser display: its refs, how actions are checked, and what each failure means.

view list.line: Lists the Views open on the operator's screen, with the ids that the other view and browser commands take.

view status.line: Shows one View by its id, so you can read what a delegated agent opened in it.

view select.line: Brings a View to the front of its area.

view close.line: Closes a View, so it leaves the operator's screen.

view split.line: Splits an area on one of its edges, so a View can sit beside the others.
view split.example: hide view split browser-3 --area area-1 --edge right

view move.line: Moves a View into another area, at the position you give.

links pr.line: Shows the projects and sessions Hide has linked to a pull request.

links issue.line: Shows the sessions and pull requests Hide has linked to a GitHub issue in this project.

links branch.line: Shows the pull requests and sessions Hide has linked to a Git branch in this project.

links session.line: Shows the pull requests and sessions Hide has linked to one session.

session list.line: Lists the recent sessions of this project and of its connected devices, one line each, with a summary.

session record.line: Shows one session as its record: its summary, its state and the requests it received.

session read.line: Reads the raw events of a session around one request, for when the exact words or tool output matter.

memory show.line: Prints one Project Memory card in full, with its status and where its words came from.

memory search.line: Finds Project Memory cards that match some words, and prints each card's number and title.

memory add.line: Saves a decision the operator made as a Project Memory card, so later agents follow it.
memory add.example: hide memory add 'Use the staging database for migration tests.'

memory forget.line: Takes a Project Memory card out of use, when the operator asks for it; memory undo brings it back.

memory undo.line: Brings back a Project Memory card that was taken out of use.

memory placed.line: Records that a Project Memory card has been written into a document at a path, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory building.line: Records that a Project Memory card is being written into a document on a branch, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory unbuilt.line: Records why a Project Memory card cannot be written into a document yet, for the agent that moves cards into documents.

memory outdated.line: Records that a document is newer than what the operator said, so the Project Memory card for it is outdated.

memory skipped.line: Records why a Project Memory card was skipped when moving cards into documents.

memory stale.line: Reports that a Project Memory card no longer matches what the operator said, so Hide stops giving it to agents until it is analyzed or released.
memory stale.example: hide memory stale m508 'The operator moved the issue template.'

memory release.line: Ends a hold that an agent's stale report put on a card, so agents get the card again.

memory recheck.line: Asks for a Project Memory card to be checked again, and keeps it out of agents' prompts until that check ends.
